scenes.tts: The first film turned molecular events into reads. How do millions of reads become one genome? Some overlap unique places. Others seem to fit several. The computer must separate missing evidence from evidence that cannot be placed.
scenes.caption: The first film turned molecular events into reads. How do millions of reads become one genome? Some overlap unique places. Others seem to fit several. The computer must separate missing evidence from evidence that cannot be placed.
scenes.visual: Reuse the first film's colour map exactly: genome and reference paths blue, reads gold, repeats red, reversible or adjustable features teal, confirmed signal green, uncertainty grey. Fill the frame with one long blue genome ribbon. Gold reads continuously drift down; some snap into one place, while others hover between grey question marks. Put a small 'schematic' label on every cartoon scene; use 'computed' only for the computed coverage curve.
scenes.narration: The first film turned molecular events into reads. How do millions of reads become one genome? Some overlap unique places. Others seem to fit several. The computer must separate missing evidence from evidence that cannot be placed.

scenes.visual: Keep the blue ribbon scrolling and gold reads landing behind a two-second title, When Reads Become a Genome. Clear the title without clearing the world.

scenes.tts: Start with sampling. Coverage is the mean number of reads lying over each base. As more gold reads land at random, blue gaps shrink. The mean does not promise equal stacks everywhere. A position can still receive many reads, few reads, or none.
scenes.caption: Start with sampling. Coverage is the mean number of reads lying over each base. As more gold reads land at random, blue gaps shrink. The mean does not promise equal stacks everywhere. A position can still receive many reads, few reads, or none.
scenes.visual: Gold reads land at reproducible pseudo-random positions along the blue ribbon. A vertical stack-height track grows above each position. Keep one uncovered blue gap visible while nearby stacks become tall. Label the track mean coverage, not uniform coverage.
scenes.narration: Start with sampling. Coverage is the mean number of reads lying over each base. As more gold reads land at random, blue gaps shrink. The mean does not promise equal stacks everywhere. A position can still receive many reads, few reads, or none.

scenes.tts: Under ideal random sampling, the unread fraction falls exponentially as mean coverage rises. Adding reads therefore attacks a sampling problem. It makes an unseen position less likely, although real libraries are less even.
scenes.caption: Under ideal random sampling, the unread fraction falls exponentially as mean coverage rises. Adding reads therefore attacks a sampling problem. It makes an unseen position less likely, although real libraries are less even.
scenes.visual: Transform the stack-height track into a large curve computed from fraction unread equals exponential of minus coverage. Animate a gold marker moving right while the grey unread fraction falls. Keep an explicit computed label. A small grey real libraries badge widens the ideal band without claiming a measured curve. Keep green only for confirmed placements.
scenes.narration: Under ideal random sampling, the unread fraction falls exponentially as mean coverage rises. Adding reads therefore attacks a sampling problem. It makes an unseen position less likely, although real libraries are less even.

scenes.tts: Now the same red repeat block appears at two places along the blue ribbon. A short gold read from inside that block matches both places equally. Its bases may be accurate, yet its address is ambiguous. More copies of that same short evidence do not create a unique address.
scenes.caption: Now the same red repeat block appears at two places along the blue ribbon. A short gold read from inside that block matches both places equally. Its bases may be accurate, yet its address is ambiguous. More copies of that same short evidence do not create a unique address.
scenes.visual: Keep one blue ribbon. Place an identical large red repeat block at two separated positions, left and right, each between different blue flanks. Label the exact-repeat model schematic. One short gold read slides between the two red blocks; both placements glow green equally, with no rejected copy. Do not draw the copies as branches or paths; branches are reserved for reference and pangenome scenes.
scenes.narration: Now the same red repeat block appears at two places along the blue ribbon. A short gold read from inside that block matches both places equally. Its bases may be accurate, yet its address is ambiguous. More copies of that same short evidence do not create a unique address.

scenes.tts: Another pile of short reads is ready to land on the repeats. Will a deeper pile tell which flanking regions belong together?
scenes.caption: Another pile of short reads is ready to land on the repeats. Will a deeper pile tell which flanking regions belong together?
scenes.visual: A stack of short gold reads waits above the two red repeat blocks on the one blue ribbon. Both possible blue-flank connections remain visible with grey question marks. The reads bob gently without landing.
scenes.narration: Another pile of short reads is ready to land on the repeats. Will a deeper pile tell which flanking regions belong together?

scenes.visual: Hold the prediction. The waiting reads drift slightly, both repeat placements pulse together, and neither flank connection is selected.

scenes.tts: The pile grows, but both placements remain possible. More reads fill sampling gaps; reads that span a repeat place it. Now one long gold read crosses the red repeat and reaches blue unique sequence on both sides. That span links the repeat copy to its flanks.
scenes.caption: The pile grows, but both placements remain possible. More reads fill sampling gaps; reads that span a repeat place it. Now one long gold read crosses the red repeat and reaches blue unique sequence on both sides. That span links the repeat copy to its flanks.
scenes.visual: Drop the waiting short reads onto both red blocks; both positions still glow equally. Merge them into one long gold read that stretches across a red block into different blue flanks on both sides. The connection glows green only when unique flanks are reached; do not mark the other copy rejected.
scenes.narration: The pile grows, but both placements remain possible. More reads fill sampling gaps; reads that span a repeat place it. Now one long gold read crosses the red repeat and reaches blue unique sequence on both sides. That span links the repeat copy to its flanks.

scenes.tts: De novo assembly joins reads without a reference, first producing contigs or an assembly graph. Reference alignment asks where reads fit on a reference path or graph already chosen. Now the reference branches. A read missing from one path can fit another. What counts as a reported difference changes with the reference.
scenes.caption: De novo assembly joins reads without a reference, first producing contigs or an assembly graph. Reference alignment asks where reads fit on a reference path or graph already chosen. Now the reference branches. A read missing from one path can fit another. What counts as a reported difference changes with the reference.
scenes.visual: Transform the resolved ribbon into a blue reference line, then branch it into two alternative blue paths. Gold reads align along each branch. A gold read that hovered off the single line now snaps onto the added branch. Green difference markers move as the active reference path changes. Label the graph schematic.
scenes.narration: De novo assembly joins reads without a reference, first producing contigs or an assembly graph. Reference alignment asks where reads fit on a reference path or graph already chosen. Now the reference branches. A read missing from one path can fit another. What counts as a reported difference changes with the reference.

scenes.tts: Long accurate reads and ultra-long spans closed difficult gaps in one human assembly. A pangenome then added alternative paths from many chromosome copies. Completeness asks whether sequence is missing. Representation asks whether one path captures human variation.
scenes.caption: Long accurate reads and ultra-long spans closed difficult gaps in one human assembly. A pangenome then added alternative paths from many chromosome copies. Completeness asks whether sequence is missing. Representation asks whether one path captures human variation.
scenes.visual: On the carried blue path, long gold reads bridge grey gaps until the line becomes continuous. Then the line expands into several blue branches, each traversed by gold reads. Keep two large labels only: completeness beside the continuous line and representation beside the branches. Mark the history diagram schematic.
scenes.narration: Long accurate reads and ultra-long spans closed difficult gaps in one human assembly. A pangenome then added alternative paths from many chromosome copies. Completeness asks whether sequence is missing. Representation asks whether one path captures human variation.

scenes.tts: Reference choice changes two stages. First, it changes whether a read has a close place to align. Then it changes which base or segment is labelled different. A variant call is therefore a comparison, not a claim about rarity, selection, or health.
scenes.caption: Reference choice changes two stages. First, it changes whether a read has a close place to align. Then it changes which base or segment is labelled different. A variant call is therefore a comparison, not a claim about rarity, selection, or health.
scenes.visual: Keep the alternative blue reference branches. One gold read aligns cleanly to one branch and poorly to the other. A green difference marker moves when the chosen path changes. Separate grey boxes labelled rarity, selection, and health remain question marks; the call does not fill them.
scenes.narration: Reference choice changes two stages. First, it changes whether a read has a close place to align. Then it changes which base or segment is labelled different. A variant call is therefore a comparison, not a claim about rarity, selection, or health.

scenes.tts: Genome results depend on what each read records and where it fits. Was the region sampled, and was the evidence placed uniquely? Extra reads help the first. Reads that span the repeat help the second. A richer reference gives reads from missing sequence a place to land. Those are different limits, and they need different fixes.

scenes.visual: Divide the carried world into two large panels. Left: gold reads fill a blue sampling gap under the label sampled. Right: one long gold read bridges a red repeat into blue flanks under the label placed. The panels transform into two green checks without implying every real region is resolved.
scenes.narration: Genome results depend on what each read records and where it fits. Was the region sampled, and was the evidence placed uniquely? Extra reads help the first. scenes.visual: End card with one line only, centred large: 'More reads fill sampling gaps; reads that span a repeat place it.' No subtitle, site name, title, or smaller line.
